caption:
Super Green Coconut Broth with Sticky Chicken & Rice 

Dinner ready in less than 30 minutes, full of flavour and absolutely no faff. 

Serves 2 
520 kcal 
38g protein 

Ingredients 
- 1 tin coconut milk 
- 2 cloves garlic
- 15g ginger 
- 1.5 tbsp Green curry Paste 
- 2 spring onions 
- 35g spinach 
- 1 tbsp honey
- 1 tbsp soy sauce 
- 1 tbsp fish sauce 

- 2 chicken thighs
- 1 tbsp honey 
- 1 tbsp sesame oil 
- 1 tbsp soy sauce 
- 1 tsp garlic powder 
- 1 tbsp hoisin sauce (optional) 

To serve (optional) 
- Pak Choy 
- Sticky Rice 
- Coriander 
- Lime 
- Sesame seeds 
- Chilli oil 

Mix the honey, soy, hoisin, sesame oil and garlic powder together. Add the chicken thighs to fully coat, then set aside. 

Add everything for the sauce to a blender and blitz until smooth, pour into a sauce pan and gently simmer for 10 minutes.

Take a frying knife and on a high heat and add a little oil. Cook the chicken thighs a couple minutes each side until charred, then turn the the heat down slightly and add any remaining marinade from the bowl to the pan and allow to bubble and thick to coat the chicken. Once cooked remove from pan and slice. 

Do not Clean the pan, add in the pak choy and cook around a minute each side to get a nice char. 

Load up your bowl. Add some cook sticky rice to the base, pour over the sauce; add the sliced chicken, Pak choy and garnish with fresh coriander, chilli oil, lime and sesame seeds

This was five minutes before we tipsily booked flights to Barcelona… 

Starring @darc_y_b and @thecocktailtradingco

Cosy Asian Cafes in London: Part 1 🍵 

I travel across the world for my favourite types of cafes so I thought I’d make a series where you can enjoy the conform of Asian cafes (this series will cover east and south) without leaving London. 

Starting off with a recent trip to @uchibake in Hackney. Uchi means house so you take your shoes off and throw on a pair of slippers just like you would in Japan. The style of the cafe transports you to Kyoto, a unique touch in London. 

I can’t remember the prices (I was too distracted by the sandos) but for 2 sandos, a creme puff, a matcha cheesecake and two different types of lattes my bill came to £28 in total, for an afternoon tea for 2 people I thought this was decently priced! 

I can’t wait to go back! Stay tuned for part 2 ❤️

⚠️ THIS IS NOT A DRILL - top tier train hack status ⚠️ and you’re still in time to use this on your Christmas trains 🚝🎄

💾 Save this for the future and tag someone who is gonna LOVE this hack

👩‍💻 Full info and how it works over on ⬇️ 
cheapholidayexpert.com (it’s currently on the homepage!)

And for now, here’s the quick debrief:

🚆Avanti Superfare matches empty seats with customers who have a bit of flexibility 
🚆This works by customers booking a ticket for their intended date of travel, but instead of selecting a time they can only select morning, afternoon or evening

🚆24 hours before their trip, Avanti will confirm what train they will be on - and assign them a seat

It’s pretty clever right?! Because Avanti can fill up their emptier trains and we can get a much cheaper seat.

Speaking of costs…

Here’s some example fares from London (one way):

🚄 London ➡️ Birmingham - £9
🚄 London ➡️ Manchester - £20
🚄 London ➡️ Liverpool - £15
🚄 London ➡️ Preston - £22

These prices are set, and work vice versa. You also don’t have to start your journey in London - these are just examples!

The main things to bear in mind are:

⚠️ You can only book between 7 - 21 days so if you’re after Christmas fares - GO GO GO
⚠️ You can’t use a railcard
⚠️ You can’t change your ticket or get a refund

Eurostar used to have something very similar called ‘Eurostar snap’ (bring it back pleeeeeease) and I’d love to see more train networks doing this 👍

Chicken & Potato Curry 🌶️🔥
Ingredients: 
- 2tbsp Oil
- 1tbsp Salt 
- 1tbsp Garlic (3 cloves Minced) 
- 1tbsp Ginger minced (use grater) 
- 1 - 1.5 Large Onion 
- 1tsp Panch Puran 
- 3 Cardamom 
- 1 Cinnamon Stick 
- 1 Bay Leaf
- 3 Pepper Corn 
- (Add 2 fresh tomatoes optional)
- 1.5 - 2tsp Extra Hot Chilli Powder 
- 1tsp Paprika 
- 1tsp - 1.5tsp Cumin 
- 1tsp Ground Coriander 
- 0.5tsp Turmeric 
- 1tsp - 1.5tsp Mixed Curry Powder 
- (Bolst Bangladeshi Brand) 
- 0.5tsp Garam Masala Powder (optional)
- 1 Whole Small Chicken (Cut into curry pieces) 
- Large cut potatoes 
- Fresh Coriander 

Recipe: 
- At medium heat, brown the garlic and ginger in the heat. Make sure to not burn it and stick to the pan 
- Add your onions, a bit of extra oil and salt, and caramelise your onions 
- This part of the process is the most tedious and takes the longest. You have to make sure not to burn it by stirring and adding bits of water to prevent burning. Use a masher to mash the onions down. Have patience in this part it’s the most important 
- Once it is a paste and the oil starts to separate, add the garam masala. And cook them off for 5 mins 
- Add the curry powders and do the same.
- Wash and prep the chicken and add to the curry paste. Stir thoroughly and cook with lid on at medium / high heat to release the water for 10 mins 
- Keep stirring and cooking 
- Once the water has released, add your potatoes and a third glass of water. Cook with the lid on until cooked through 
- If it seems too thick, keep adding water or allow to simmer. 
- Allow the oil to separate and settle and add coriander off the heat

HIGH PROTEIN BREAKFAST WRAP for Episode 14 of my ongoing BREAKFAST CLUB series!

A riff on my viral soy sauce scallion eggs, this version comes loaded with the most delicious sauces and packed in a high protein wrap for a substantive dish that’s just as good for dinner as it is at breakfast.

Start by gently heating a splash of oil. Stir in 2-3 tsp chilli flakes/ gochugaru + 2-3 tsp sesame seeds .

Once fragrant , stir in a handful of sliced onions and green onions. Sauté for a few minutes.

Then crack in two eggs. Once they’ve started to cook, cover with a tortilla (I’m using almond wrap!), gently pressing down to set.

Then flip and add 1 tbsp soy sauce + Mayo + hot sauce (measure with  your soul!).

🧙🏻‍♀️ Harry Potter Themed Tea 🫖

In honor of Harry Potter’s birthday, thought it was fitting to post about the “Magical World of Afternoon Tea” I did earlier this month at Drink Me Tea Room. 

They do it twice a year (January and July) and reservations get booked out FAST. We did the Full Wizard’s Tea, but there’s levels below that (they even have a Leaky Cauldron Tipsy Tea if you prefer cocktails). 

Under their Special Tea Potions section they even have fun cocktails like butterbeer, gillyweed, and “Dragons!? The first task is dragons?” (you get to pick a dragon from a bag that determines your cocktail of choice!). They have mocktail versions of most of their drinks as well. 

If you’re a Harry Potter fan I highly recommend doing this when you can (I didn’t post about it earlier since sadly reservations got booked out immediately). They always do an Alice in Wonderland theme, but have rotating themes year around (in August they’re doing Star Wars 👀).
